# Project workflow

Read AGENTS.md for the project workflow and Beads skill.

○ trial-tfh · Adopt the provider's protocol 2 contract   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner  
  approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:    
                                                                              
  Protocol 2: the pair (account_id, delivery_id) identifies a delivery; the   
  same delivery_id under a different account identifies a separate delivery.  
  Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt   
  with the latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest    
  record_id. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each        
  accepted receipt retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and       
  payload. Present accepted receipts in their original input order. This      
  identity contract comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation          
  guarantee; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee.        
                                                                              
  Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit       
  "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the  
  original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol
  used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of    
  receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and
  zero duplicates.

Courier Relay: cross-account delivery identity contract (established for trial-ewy, summary command, protocol "1").

delivery_id values are only guaranteed unique within a single account's receipts, not globally. When a request spans multiple accounts (e.g. the "summary" command), delivery identity for accept/duplicate purposes is the pair (account_id, delivery_id), not delivery_id alone. Two receipts with the same delivery_id but different account_id are distinct deliveries and never count as duplicates of each other.

Within one identity group, the accepted receipt is chosen the same way as the single-account "count" command: earliest occurred_at (compared as a UTC instant) wins, ties broken by the lexicographically (Unicode code-point) smallest record_id. All other receipts in the group are duplicates.

accepted_count = number of distinct (account_id, delivery_id) keys present; duplicate_count = total receipts - accepted_count. Empty batch -> 0/0.

Any future command that aggregates receipts across accounts (not just "summary") should use this same (account_id, delivery_id) identity unless a new approval explicitly overrides it. The single-account "count" command is unaffected and keeps deduping by delivery_id alone, since it operates on one account's receipts.

Basis: issue trial-ewy description ("Account attribution and delivery identity must follow that contract") plus no prior memory existed on this topic; this record establishes the contract going forward. Implemented in main.py via a shared dedupe(receipts, key_fn) helper.

Memories matching "courier-relay":

  courier-relay/cross-account-delivery-identity
    Courier Relay: cross-account delivery identity contract (established for trial-ewy, summary command, protocol "1").  ...

Store a memory that persists across sessions and account rotations.

Memories are injected at prime time (bd prime) so you have them
in every session without manual loading.

The positional arg is the memory CONTENT (the key is auto-generated from it
unless --key is given). As a convenience, if the arg is a bare key naming an
existing memory, it is RECALLED instead of stored (same as 'bd recall');
a bare key naming nothing is refused. Use --key to store slug-like content.

Examples:
  bd remember "always run tests with -race flag"
  bd remember "Dolt phantom DBs hide in three places" --key dolt-phantoms
  bd remember "auth module uses JWT not sessions" --key auth-jwt
  bd remember dolt-phantoms        # bare existing key: reads it (= bd recall)

Usage:
  bd remember "<insight>" [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help         help for remember
      --key string   Explicit key for the memory (auto-generated from content if not set). If a memory with this key already exists, it will be updated in place

Global Flags:
      --actor string              Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)
      --cpu-profile               Generate CPU profile for performance analysis
      --database string           Run against a different server database for this invocation, without changing the project's configured database (proxied-server mode only)
      --db string                 Database path (default: auto-discover .beads/*.db). In proxied-server mode, a value that isn't an existing path is treated as a database name override (see --database)
  -C, --directory string          Change to this directory before running the command (like git -C)
      --dolt-auto-commit string   Dolt auto-commit policy (off|on|batch). 'on': commit after each write. 'batch': defer commits to bd dolt commit; uncommitted changes persist in the working set until then (a live batch-mode bd process also flushes on SIGTERM/SIGHUP). Applies to embedded and direct SQL-server modes; proxied-server routes are unaffected. Default: on. Override via config key dolt.auto-commit
      --global                    Use the global shared-server database (beads_global)
      --ignore-schema-skew        Proceed despite forward schema drift (some queries may fail)
      --json                      Output in JSON format
      --mem-profile string        Write heap profile to FILE on exit (also respects BEADS_MEM_PROFILE)
      --no-color                  Disable color output (also: NO_COLOR=1 or CLICOLOR=0)
  -q, --quiet                     Suppress non-essential output (errors only)
      --readonly                  Read-only mode: block write operations (for worker sandboxes)
      --sandbox                   Sandbox mode: disables Dolt auto-push
  -v, --verbose                   Enable verbose/debug output

Courier Relay: delivery identity and acceptance-rule contract across protocol versions (identity established for trial-ewy on protocol "1"; acceptance rule revised for trial-tfh with permanent adoption of protocol "2" as current).

Identity (unchanged by protocol version): for the "summary" command, which spans multiple accounts, delivery identity for accept/duplicate purposes is the pair (account_id, delivery_id), not delivery_id alone -- the same delivery_id under a different account_id is a separate delivery and never a duplicate of it. This comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it. The single-account "count" command is unaffected and keeps deduping by delivery_id alone, since it operates on one account's receipts; that policy is a code-simplicity choice for count's single-account inputs, not a different identity rule.

Acceptance rule, protocol "1" (still explicitly supported, no longer current): within one identity group, the accepted receipt is the one with the EARLIEST occurred_at (compared as a UTC instant); ties broken by the lexicographically (Unicode code-point) smallest record_id. All other receipts in the group are duplicates.

Acceptance rule, protocol "2" (current as of trial-tfh; provider permanently adopted this contract, approved by the integration owner): within one identity group, the accepted receipt is the one with the LATEST occurred_at (UTC instant); ties still broken by smallest record_id. All other receipts in the group are duplicates. This is the only behavioral change from protocol "1" -- identity grouping is identical.

Protocol selection: an omitted "protocol" field selects the current protocol (now "2"). Explicit "protocol":"1" or "protocol":"2" selects that version's rule set exactly as described above; both remain supported so protocol "1" requests keep working after "2" became current. accepted_count = number of distinct identity-group keys present; duplicate_count = total receipts - accepted_count. Empty batch -> 0/0. This same latest-wins/earliest-wins distinction and identity contract applies to both "count" and "summary" for protocol 2, per trial-tfh's explicit instruction to update both commands.

Basis: trial-ewy issue description (identity contract) and trial-tfh issue description (protocol 2 permanent adoption, integration-owner approval, "update count and summary" instruction). Implemented in main.py via a shared dedupe(receipts, key_fn, protocol) helper; protocol selects latest_wins vs earliest_wins, key_fn selects delivery_id (count) or (account_id, delivery_id) (summary).
